definitions.explanation: Cheap relative to what you get, or cheaper compared to alternatives. Implies good value for money.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{割安|わりやす}でおいしい。
examples.english: This restaurant is affordable and delicious.

examples.japanese: まとめ{買|が}いすると{割安|わりやす}になる。
examples.english: Buying in bulk makes it cheaper per unit.

examples.japanese: {平日|へいじつ}のランチは{夜|よる}に{比|くら}べて{割安|わりやす}な{値段|ねだん}で{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: Weekday lunches can be enjoyed at more affordable prices compared to dinner.

notes:
{割安|わりやす} means relatively cheap or good value for the price. It emphasizes that something is cheaper than expected or compared to alternatives, not just cheap in absolute terms.

FORMS:
{割|わり} (ratio, proportion) + {安|やす} (cheap) — cheap relative to the value you get.
- Na-adjective: {割安|わりやす}な{商品|しょうひん} (a good-value product)
- Noun: {割安|わりやす}{感|かん} (sense of being a good deal)
- Adverbial: {割安|わりやす}に{買|か}える (can buy at a good price)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {割安|わりやす}な{値段|ねだん} (affordable/bargain price)
- まとめ{買|が}いすると{割安|わりやす} (buying in bulk is cheaper per unit)
- {割安|わりやす}{株|かぶ} (undervalued stock — in finance)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- Opposite: {割高|わりだか} (relatively expensive, poor value for money)
- {安|やす}い is simply 'cheap,' while {割安|わりやす} implies good value relative to quality or alternatives
